title: Deterministic transliteration engine: NFC normalization, grapheme-cluster segmentation, ordered context-sensitive rules (forward + inverse)
context: open-transliteration's reference engine is the thin, deterministic interpreter that applies mapping scheme data in both the forward and inverse directions. It must be NFC-correct by construction, operate on extended grapheme clusters (not code points), produce deterministic output, and contain no ML, no vendor/agent-specific logic, and no network calls at runtime. It loads and validates schemes against mappingSchemeSchema. This is the core runtime that all scheme data and test tasks depend on.
objective: Implement transliterate(text, schemeId, direction), loadScheme(id), and checkReversible(schemeId) in packages/core with a pipeline of: NFC-normalize → segment into extended grapheme clusters (via Intl.Segmenter or a vetted grapheme library) → apply ordered context-sensitive rules (first match within a cluster) → emit. Provide a symmetric inverse path. Expose a thin CLI command (transliterate <scheme> <direction>) for batch use.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/core exports transliterate(text, schemeId, direction), loadScheme(id), and checkReversible(schemeId) as ESM-compatible TypeScript with no vendor-specific imports

Pipeline is: NFC-normalize → segment into extended grapheme clusters → apply ordered rules (first match within a cluster, context-sensitive where contextBefore/contextAfter defined) → emit; identical pipeline applies in both forward and inverse directions
Engine loads and validates schemes against mappingSchemeSchema at load time; throws a typed error for invalid schemes
No ML, no network calls, no vendor/agent-specific logic in packages/core; purely deterministic

Unit tests cover: NFC normalization of composed/decomposed input, combining-mark handling, context-before and context-after rules, passthrough of digits/punctuation/foreign-text not in the rule set, and empty/boundary inputs
CLI command transliterate <scheme> <direction> reads stdin and writes stdout for batch use
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint passes
resources: PLAN.md — Solution approach & architecture (engine pipeline, packages/core)
output: packages/core/src/engine.ts (or equivalent ESM module) + packages/core/src/cli.ts; unit tests in packages/core/src/__tests__/; updated pnpm workspace build
